```c
size = proto_signature_length + (unsigned int)ntohs(hdr->len);

But what if `hdr->fam` is TCP4 (0x11) and `hdr->len` is 36? The check passes (size = 52 <= 52). The code reads `hdr->addr.ip4.*` which is 12 bytes starting at offset 16. So it reads up to offset 28. This is within the struct (which is 52 bytes). Then `buffer += 52`, which advances the buffer by 52 bytes.

But the actual PROXY header data is only 16 + 12 = 28 bytes. So the buffer pointer is advanced by 24 extra bytes. This means the HTTP parser will start parsing at the wrong position.

But this isn't a buffer overflow. It's just incorrect parsing.
